messages.subject: y-axis text overplots ontop of plot
parts:
Hello,

Somehow, my y-axis text behaves a bit weird. As you can see on the
picture (see link below), the text reaches into the plot. At the same
time the distance to the y-axis title is extremely large. I do not
really want to change the size of the text as the plots are generated
in a large script and share settings...
Is there a way to handle this differently?

http://dl.dropbox.com/u/1414944/ggoverplot.jpg

Thanks
jorgusch

messages.subject: Re: y-axis text overplots ontop of plot
parts:
Hi Hardley,

I am sorry, I should have done that.
Below you find the code for my problem and over night I just thought
of something: Is there a way to define the plot areas like in HTML?
Twenty precent for y-axis.title, 15% for y.axis.text ,65% for plot.
same for vertical space aka x...?

I might be too stupid (as many other posters asking familiar
questions ;-), but this object specific definitions seem to be a big
pain.

Thanks for help!

library("ggplot2")

cX <- rep(c(1:20),2)
cY <- c((-20:19)/10000)
mydata <- data.frame(cbind(cX,cY))

myTheme<-function() {
textsize<-15
labelsize<-14
structure(list(
panel.background = theme_rect(colour = "white"),
panel.grid.major = theme_line(colour = "lightgray", size = 0.8),
panel.grid.minor = theme_line(colour = "lightgray"),
# axis.line = theme_line(colour = "lightgray"), # does not work
as well...
axis.text.x = theme_text(size = labelsize, face = "bold"),
axis.title.x = theme_text(size = textsize),
axis.text.y = theme_text(size = labelsize, face = "bold"),
axis.title.y = theme_text(size = textsize),
axis.ticks = theme_blank()
), class = "options")
}


p <- ggplot(mydata, aes(x=mydata[,1], y=mydata[,2])) +
geom_point(alpha = 1/5) + myTheme() + geom_smooth()
print(p + opts(title = "Something that overplots and title changes
with every plot"))
